mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 1.5% for three consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future corporate earnings, lowering the present value of expected cash flows and thus depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 30-day pre-trend window (p > 0.05), or the 3-month FEDFUNDS decline is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative despite the labor indicators meeting the trigger, or the correlation between PAYEMS/UNRATE and SPX 20d returns falls below 0.3 in a 60-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures ( proxy via GDPC1 ) exceeding 3% suggests accelerating demand growth that outpaces supply, pushing up future earnings expectations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) or SPX 5d returns are not positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month indicates supply-side weakness, prompting market participants to anticipate future production shortfalls and bid up equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 5% in a single month
failure_condition: INDPRO does not revert to growth or SPX 20d returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 0.3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to respond with negative forward returns over the next 60 days as markets anticipate a potential rate hike cycle.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL does not exceed 0.3% for two months or SPX 20d returns are not significantly negative (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in job openings ( proxy via HOUST ) and a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) by at least 0.2 percentage points indicates a cooling labor market, reducing optimism and pushing down S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by > 10% while UNRATE increases by > 0.2pp in the same month
failure_condition: HOUST does not fall or UNRATE does not rise as predicted, or SPX 20d returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 248) and steady FEDFUNDS (< 1.5%), S&P 500 forward returns tend to be positive over the next 20 days due to reduced policy uncertainty and improved risk sentiment.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are not positive or the regime condition persists for < 30 days and returns remain non-positive.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid and persistent decline in RSAFS below 450 billion dollars indicates weakening financial conditions that trigger a flight to quality in equities, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by > 50 billion in a single month
failure_condition: RSAFS does not decline as predicted or SPX 5d returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).
